commands.name: RUVIO
commands.limitations: No arguments replies PONG is taken. OWNER names the shard rule. RUVIO TOPOLOGY VERSION returns the cluster map version the node serves (0 without cluster_topology); RUVIO TOPOLOGY SET map installs a newer map (sent by ruvio coordinator; @admin @dangerous; a slot may join the node's group only once RUVIO MIGRATE prepared its data there). RUVIO MIGRATE IMPORT, EXPORT, COPY, PREPARE, CANCEL and STATUS move a slot range between groups for ruvio coordinator (COORDINATOR MOVE; @admin @dangerous; AUTH arguments redacted in SLOWLOG); see docs/COMPATIBILITY.md. Any other argument is an error.

commands.name: HELLO
commands.limitations: HELLO and HELLO 2 or 3. AUTH username password and SETNAME are accepted after the version. An unknown version returns NOPROTO and changes nothing. Attributes are not produced.

commands.name: AUTH
commands.limitations: Default user or configured ACL users. AUTH username password is supported.

commands.name: ACL WHOAMI
commands.limitations: The name copied at the last AUTH.

commands.name: ACL USERS
commands.limitations: Live directory, including ACL SETUSER users until restart.

commands.name: ACL LIST
commands.limitations: Passwords are redacted. Includes ACL SETUSER users until restart.

commands.name: ACL GETUSER
commands.limitations: Flat bulk fields. Passwords are counted, not echoed. Reads the live directory.

commands.name: ACL CAT
commands.limitations: Ruvio command categories only.

commands.name: ACL SETUSER
commands.limitations: Incremental rules. A new user starts off with no password, commands, or keys. A failed rule changes nothing. Open connections keep the rules from their last AUTH. ACL SAVE writes the live directory when security.acl_file is set. Rules must be UTF-8.

commands.name: ACL LOAD
commands.limitations: Replaces the live directory from security.acl_file. A missing path or a bad line changes nothing. Open connections keep the rules from their last AUTH. GET and SET do not read the file.

commands.name: ACL SAVE
commands.limitations: Writes the live directory to security.acl_file, including passwords. ACL LIST stays redacted. A missing path changes nothing.

commands.name: GET
commands.limitations: WRONGTYPE on a non-string key.

commands.name: SETV
commands.limitations: Writes a versioned string. The first call with no version creates version 1. A later call must pass the current version and receives the next one. A mismatch returns an error and does not change the value. A plain SET replaces the versioned string. The version is stored only on keys written with SETV, and that write is a WAL record.

commands.name: TAKE
commands.limitations: Subtracts a positive count from an integer when the key holds at least that many. Returns the remainder. A missing key or a shortfall returns a null bulk and does not create or change the key. The successful subtraction is the same integer WAL record as INCR. A non-integer is WRONGTYPE.

commands.name: TRANSFER
commands.limitations: TRANSFER source destination amount [MAX cap] subtracts a positive amount from the integer at source when it holds at least that much and adds it to destination, creating destination at amount when it is missing. Returns [source after, destination after]. A missing or short source, an addition that overflows, or a destination that would pass MAX returns a null bulk and writes nothing. Source and destination must differ and share a slot. Both keys are written as one WAL record. A non-integer is an error and a key of another type is WRONGTYPE.

commands.name: HTRANSFER
commands.limitations: HTRANSFER key from to amount [MAX cap] is TRANSFER between two fields of one hash. Returns [from after, to after], or a null bulk when the key or the from field is missing or short, the addition overflows, or to would pass MAX; nothing is written then. A missing to field is created at amount. Field TTLs stay. Both fields are written as one WAL record. A field that is not an integer is an error.

commands.name: DELEX
commands.limitations: Ruvio extension. `DELEX key IFEQ value` deletes the string only when it equals `value` and returns 1, otherwise 0. A missing key returns 0; another type is WRONGTYPE. The delete is the ordinary `DEL` WAL record.

commands.name: GETEX
commands.limitations: Returns the string and sets its deadline to now plus the given milliseconds. A missing key returns a null bulk and stores nothing. GET does not move a deadline. The deadline is the existing expire WAL record. A non-string is WRONGTYPE.

commands.name: LIMIT
commands.limitations: Fixed window on one key. Returns the remaining allowance after this call, or a null bulk when the window is full. The counter is not incremented on rejection. SLIDING keeps a weighted count of the current and previous window (maximum up to 2147483647), TOKENS a token bucket of `max` tokens that refills over the window (capacity up to 1000000, refill up to 4294967295 ms, COST n takes n tokens); a refused call writes nothing. WITHRETRY returns [remaining, retry_after_ms] with remaining -1 when refused. A key keeps the mode it was created with: another mode on it is an error. The window is the key deadline, so an unused window disappears. A plain key does not store a limit. The accepted call is a WAL record. GET of a limit is WRONGTYPE.

commands.name: IDEM
commands.limitations: IDEM key BEGIN fingerprint owner ttl_ms atomically reserves a missing key or returns pending, conflict, or completed with the binary result. IDEM key COMPLETE fingerprint owner result publishes only for the matching live owner. Identical completion is acknowledged without rewriting; changed results are refused. Neither retries nor completion renew the original TTL. Tokens are 1-128 bytes, retention is 1 ms-7 days, and result is at most 4 MiB (also subject to protocol limits including the packed metadata). Uses the existing string layout with an internal packed record; do not modify it with string/expiry commands. Each state transition and its deadline is one WAL record. Not exactly-once for external effects.

commands.name: ONCE
commands.limitations: First call returns 1 and keeps the key until the TTL. A later call returns 0 and does not refresh the TTL. After the deadline the next call is first again. The marker exists only on keys written with ONCE. The first call is a WAL record. GET of an once key is WRONGTYPE.

commands.name: LEASE
commands.limitations: Acquires a shard-owned lease. Returns a new fencing token, or a null bulk when the lease is still held. Tokens only grow: after expiry, RELEASE, DEL, a restart, a failover or a slot move, the next grant is larger (generation in the top bits, then a counter with a clock floor). The grant is a WAL record. GET of a lease is WRONGTYPE. Unused keys do not store a lease.

commands.name: SEMAPHORE
commands.limitations: SEMAPHORE key max ttl_ms returns a token while fewer than max holders are live, or a null bulk when full. Each holder has its own TTL. RELEASE key token frees one slot. The key stores 16 bytes per live holder and goes away with the last one. Grant and release are WAL records. GET of a semaphore is WRONGTYPE.

commands.name: RELEASE
commands.limitations: Releases a lease when the token matches the current holder. Returns 1 or 0. A mismatch leaves the holder in place. The next LEASE gets a larger token. The release is a WAL record.

commands.name: RENEW
commands.limitations: RENEW key token ttl_ms moves the deadline of a live LEASE holder or SEMAPHORE slot to now + ttl_ms (the new TTL replaces the remaining time). Returns 1, or 0 when the token is expired, released or not the holder. It never creates a holder and never changes the token sequence. A lease renew is a LeasePut record and a semaphore renew a SemaphoreAcquire record with the same token, so no new WAL record type exists. Any other key type is WRONGTYPE.

commands.name: CHANGES
commands.limitations: CHANGES START arms an in-memory feed on this shard and returns the cursor. CHANGES cursor reads notes after that cursor, at most 1024. Nothing is recorded before START. The feed is not a second copy of the WAL and is empty after restart.

commands.name: SET
commands.limitations: Supports EX, PX, EXAT, PXAT, KEEPTTL, NX, XX, and GET. GET returns the previous string and refuses a non-string. `SET key value IFEQ expected [EX|PX|EXAT|PXAT|KEEPTTL]` (Ruvio extension) writes only when the string equals `expected` and answers nil otherwise; it does not combine with NX, XX or GET. `SET key value IFGT|IFLT [EX|PX|EXAT|PXAT|KEEPTTL]` (Ruvio extension) writes when the key is missing or `value` is greater (`IFGT`) or smaller (`IFLT`) than the stored signed 64-bit integer, and answers nil otherwise; a `value` or stored string that is not an integer is an error and writes nothing; it does not combine with NX, XX, GET or IFEQ.

commands.name: MGET
commands.limitations: Nil bulk for a missing or wrong-type key. Same-slot keys in multi-shard mode.

commands.name: MSET
commands.limitations: Clears TTL. Same-slot keys in multi-shard mode.

commands.name: GETSET
commands.limitations: Clears TTL. WRONGTYPE on a non-string key.

commands.name: APPEND
commands.limitations: Keeps an existing TTL.

commands.name: INCR
commands.limitations: Signed 64-bit decimal integers. `EX seconds` or `PX milliseconds` sets a deadline only when the call creates the key; an existing key keeps its deadline. The write and the deadline are one WAL record.

commands.name: DECR
commands.limitations: Signed 64-bit decimal integers. `EX seconds` or `PX milliseconds` sets a deadline only when the call creates the key; an existing key keeps its deadline. The write and the deadline are one WAL record.

commands.name: INCRBY
commands.limitations: Signed 64-bit decimal integers. INCRBY key n MAX limit returns a null bulk and writes nothing when the result would pass limit. `EX seconds` or `PX milliseconds` sets a deadline only when the call creates the key; an existing key keeps its deadline. The write and the deadline are one WAL record. Order with `MAX`: `[EX|PX] [MAX]`.

commands.name: DECRBY
commands.limitations: Signed 64-bit decimal integers. `EX seconds` or `PX milliseconds` sets a deadline only when the call creates the key; an existing key keeps its deadline. The write and the deadline are one WAL record.

commands.name: DEL
commands.limitations: Same-slot keys in multi-shard mode.

commands.name: UNLINK
commands.limitations: Synchronous, identical to DEL.

commands.name: EXISTS
commands.limitations: Same-slot keys in multi-shard mode.

commands.name: RENAME
commands.limitations: Same-slot keys in multi-shard mode.

commands.name: SCAN
commands.limitations: Shard-local. Cursors walk sorted live keys, not Redis dict cursors. Ruvio adds SLOT n (0-16383): only keys of that hash slot, run on the shard that owns it from any port; COUNT still bounds the work, so pages may be short or empty until the cursor returns 0. No CLUSTER COUNTKEYSINSLOT or GETKEYSINSLOT.

commands.name: DBSIZE
commands.limitations: Shard-local. Counts keys in the selected logical database.

commands.name: SELECT
commands.limitations: Indexes 0 through databases - 1 (16 by default, at most 256). Cluster mode allows only 0. Each database is its own map in the shard; WAL records carry the database. Routing hashes the user key. Not scriptable.

commands.name: FLUSHDB
commands.limitations: Clears the selected database on every shard. ASYNC runs synchronously. One WAL record. Allowed inside MULTI; refused in scripts.

commands.name: FLUSHALL
commands.limitations: Clears every database. ASYNC runs synchronously. One WAL record. Allowed inside MULTI; refused in scripts.

commands.name: SWAPDB
commands.limitations: O(1) map exchange, one WAL record. Allowed inside MULTI; refused in cluster mode and in scripts. Does not wake clients blocked on keys that now exist.

commands.name: MOVE
commands.limitations: One WAL record. Refused in cluster mode and in scripts. Returns 0 when the key is missing or the target already has it.

commands.name: EXPIRE
commands.limitations: A relative expire of zero or less deletes the key and returns 1, as Redis does. Accepts one of `NX`, `XX`, `GT`, `LT` (a key without a deadline counts as infinite). A condition that does not hold replies 0.

commands.name: PEXPIRE
commands.limitations: A relative expire of zero or less deletes the key and returns 1, as Redis does. Accepts one of `NX`, `XX`, `GT`, `LT` (a key without a deadline counts as infinite). A condition that does not hold replies 0.

commands.name: EXPIREAT
commands.limitations: A deadline in the past leaves the key absent and still replies OK. Accepts one of `NX`, `XX`, `GT`, `LT` (a key without a deadline counts as infinite). A condition that does not hold replies 0.

commands.name: PEXPIREAT
commands.limitations: A deadline in the past leaves the key absent and still replies OK. Accepts one of `NX`, `XX`, `GT`, `LT` (a key without a deadline counts as infinite). A condition that does not hold replies 0.

commands.name: LPUSHCAP
commands.limitations: Ruvio extension. `LPUSHCAP key cap value...` pushes like `LPUSH`, then drops items from the tail until at most `cap` remain, and returns the new length. A list already over `cap` takes one trim record; otherwise each dropped item is a pop record.

commands.name: RPUSHCAP
commands.limitations: Ruvio extension. `RPUSHCAP key cap value...` pushes like `RPUSH`, then drops items from the head until at most `cap` remain, and returns the new length.

commands.name: LPOP
commands.limitations: Optional positive COUNT returns an array. An empty list returns nil. Each popped element is its own list-pop record.

commands.name: RPOP
commands.limitations: Optional positive COUNT returns an array. An empty list returns nil. Each popped element is its own list-pop record.

commands.name: BLPOP
commands.limitations: Shard-local. At most 1,024 blocked clients per shard.

commands.name: BRPOP
commands.limitations: Shard-local. At most 1,024 blocked clients per shard.

commands.name: SMEMBERS
commands.limitations: Replies are sorted.

commands.name: SINTER
commands.limitations: Replies are sorted. Same-slot keys in multi-shard mode.

commands.name: SUNION
commands.limitations: Replies are sorted. Same-slot keys in multi-shard mode.

commands.name: SDIFF
commands.limitations: Replies are sorted. Same-slot keys in multi-shard mode.

commands.name: SINTERSTORE
commands.limitations: Same-slot keys in multi-shard mode.

commands.name: SUNIONSTORE
commands.limitations: Same-slot keys in multi-shard mode.

commands.name: SDIFFSTORE
commands.limitations: Same-slot keys in multi-shard mode.

commands.name: SMOVE
commands.limitations: Same-slot keys in multi-shard mode.

commands.name: SPOP
commands.limitations: One member without a count, or an array with a count. The removed members are recorded so recovery does not draw again.

commands.name: SRANDMEMBER
commands.limitations: Does not remove members. No count returns one bulk or nil. A positive count returns distinct members up to the set size. A negative count may repeat. Count 0 is an empty array.

commands.name: HSET
commands.limitations: Compact pairs until 64 fields or a 64-byte field/value.

commands.name: HMSET
commands.limitations: Same as multi-field HSET (Redis marks HMSET deprecated); replies OK instead of the count of new fields.

commands.name: HGETALL
commands.limitations: Enumeration order is unspecified, as in Redis.

commands.name: HKEYS
commands.limitations: Enumeration order is unspecified, as in Redis.

commands.name: HVALS
commands.limitations: Enumeration order is unspecified, as in Redis.

commands.name: HINCRBY
commands.limitations: Stores the decimal result. Non-integers and overflow are rejected without a write. `EX seconds` or `PX milliseconds` sets a deadline only when the call creates the key; an existing key keeps its deadline. The write and the deadline are one WAL record. The deadline is the key's.

commands.name: HSETNX
commands.limitations: Returns 1 and records one field when the field is missing. Returns 0 with no write when the field exists.

commands.name: HSTRLEN
commands.limitations: Returns the field length, or 0 when the key or field is missing.

commands.name: HSCAN
commands.limitations: Cursor pages follow storage order. MATCH and COUNT are supported. A missing key returns cursor 0 and an empty array.

commands.name: HEXPIRE
commands.limitations: NX, XX, GT, and LT. Replies per field: -2 missing, 0 condition not met, 1 set, 2 deleted by a zero or past time. Absolute deadline up to 2^46-1 ms. HSET and HDEL drop a field TTL; HINCRBY keeps it.

commands.name: HPEXPIRE
commands.limitations: Milliseconds. Same replies and conditions as HEXPIRE.

commands.name: HEXPIREAT
commands.limitations: Unix seconds. A past time deletes the field (reply 2).

commands.name: HPEXPIREAT
commands.limitations: Unix milliseconds. A past time deletes the field (reply 2).

commands.name: HTTL
commands.limitations: Seconds, rounded up. -1 for a field without a TTL. Missing field or key is -2. A hash with no field TTL pays nothing; the first TTL moves it to a timed form, the last HPERSIST moves it back.

commands.name: HPTTL
commands.limitations: Milliseconds. -1 for a field without a TTL. Missing field or key is -2. A hash with no field TTL pays nothing; the first TTL moves it to a timed form, the last HPERSIST moves it back.

commands.name: HEXPIRETIME
commands.limitations: Unix seconds, rounded up. -1 for a field without a TTL.

commands.name: HPEXPIRETIME
commands.limitations: Unix milliseconds. -1 for a field without a TTL.

commands.name: HPERSIST
commands.limitations: 1 removed a TTL, -1 had none, -2 missing.

commands.name: ZADD
commands.limitations: NX, XX, GT, LT, CH, and INCR. Without CH the reply counts new members. INCR returns the new score or nil. GT and LT still add a missing member. `EX seconds` or `PX milliseconds` sets a deadline only when the call creates the key; an existing key keeps its deadline. The write and the deadline are one WAL record. Placed with the other options before the first score.

commands.name: ZRANGE
commands.limitations: WITHSCORES, BYSCORE, BYLEX, REV, and LIMIT. BYSCORE and BYLEX accept LIMIT. A negative LIMIT count returns the rest of the range.

commands.name: ZREVRANGE
commands.limitations: WITHSCORES is supported.

commands.name: ZRANGEBYSCORE
commands.limitations: Supports -inf/+inf, exclusive ( bounds, and LIMIT. A negative LIMIT count returns the rest of the range.

commands.name: ZRANGEBYLEX
commands.limitations: Bounds are -, +, [member, and (member. Member order ignores the score. LIMIT is supported. A negative count returns the rest of the range.

commands.name: ZREVRANGEBYLEX
commands.limitations: The first bound is the high member and the second is the low member. Same bound and LIMIT rules as ZRANGEBYLEX.

commands.name: ZINCRBY
commands.limitations: Records the resulting score. `EX seconds` or `PX milliseconds` sets a deadline only when the call creates the key; an existing key keeps its deadline. The write and the deadline are one WAL record.

commands.name: ZPOPMIN
commands.limitations: Optional count. A flat member, score array; empty array for a missing key or count 0. Recorded as one ZREM of the popped members.

commands.name: ZPOPMAX
commands.limitations: Highest scores first. Same reply and record as ZPOPMIN.

commands.name: ZPOPBYSCORE
commands.limitations: Ruvio extension. `ZPOPBYSCORE key max [MIN min] [COUNT n] [WITHSCORES]` removes and returns up to `n` (default 1, at most 10000) members with `min <= score <= max`, lowest score first. Bounds take `-inf`, `+inf` and `(` exclusive forms. Empty array when nothing is due. Recorded as one ZREM of the popped members.

commands.name: ZMOVEDUE
commands.limitations: Ruvio extension. `ZMOVEDUE source destination max [COUNT n]` moves up to `n` (default 1, at most 10000) members with `score <= max`, lowest first, from a sorted set to the tail of a list, and returns how many moved. Source and destination must hash to the same slot. Clients blocked on the destination list are served first. Recorded as one transaction.

commands.name: BZPOPMIN
commands.limitations: Shard-local, like BLPOP. Replies key, member, score. ZADD, ZINCRBY, and GEOADD serve the oldest waiting client. At most 1,024 blocked clients per shard.

commands.name: BZPOPMAX
commands.limitations: Highest score. Otherwise as BZPOPMIN.

commands.name: ZREMRANGEBYRANK
commands.limitations: Negative ranks count from the end. Recorded as one ZREM.

commands.name: ZREMRANGEBYSCORE
commands.limitations: -inf/+inf and exclusive ( bounds. Recorded as one ZREM.

commands.name: ZREMRANGEBYLEX
commands.limitations: -, +, [member, and (member. Recorded as one ZREM.

commands.name: GEOADD
commands.limitations: One sorted set. Score is the 52-bit geohash. NX, XX, and CH. `EX seconds` or `PX milliseconds` sets a deadline only when the call creates the key; an existing key keeps its deadline. The write and the deadline are one WAL record. Placed with the other options before the first longitude.

commands.name: GEODIST
commands.limitations: Units M, KM, FT, and MI. Missing member is nil.

commands.name: GEOHASH
commands.limitations: 11-character string. The last character is 0.

commands.name: GEOPOS
commands.limitations: Missing member is nil.

commands.name: GEOSEARCH
commands.limitations: FROMMEMBER, FROMLONLAT, BYRADIUS, BYBOX, ASC, DESC, COUNT, ANY, WITHDIST, WITHHASH, WITHCOORD.

commands.name: GEOSEARCHSTORE
commands.limitations: Replaces the destination sorted set. STOREDIST stores the distance.

commands.name: GEORADIUS
commands.limitations: STORE and STOREDIST replace the destination. Same-slot when storing.

commands.name: GEORADIUSBYMEMBER
commands.limitations: STORE and STOREDIST replace the destination. Same-slot when storing.

commands.name: BF.RESERVE
commands.limitations: RedisBloom wire shape: `BF.RESERVE key error capacity [EXPANSION n | NONSCALING]`. Filters scale by default (each new layer is `expansion` times larger with half the error rate); a layer above 64 MiB is refused. Not certified module compatibility.

commands.name: BF.ADD
commands.limitations: RedisBloom wire shape. A missing key becomes a scalable filter (error 0.01, capacity 100, expansion 2). A full non-scaling filter answers an error. Not certified module compatibility.

commands.name: BF.MADD
commands.limitations: RedisBloom wire shape. One reply per item (1 added, 0 present, or an error element when a non-scaling filter is full). One WAL record for the whole batch.

commands.name: BF.INSERT
commands.limitations: RedisBloom wire shape: `CAPACITY`, `ERROR`, `EXPANSION`, `NOCREATE`, `NONSCALING`, `ITEMS`. The creation options apply only when the key is new. `NOCREATE` on a missing key answers `ERR not found`. `EX seconds` or `PX milliseconds` sets a deadline only when the call creates the key; an existing key keeps its deadline. The write and the deadline are one WAL record. Placed with the creation options before `ITEMS`.

commands.name: BF.INFO
commands.limitations: RedisBloom wire shape: Capacity, Size, Number of filters, Number of items inserted, Expansion rate (nil for a non-scaling filter); or one field by name. Size is the bit arrays plus the filter header.

commands.name: BF.CARD
commands.limitations: Items added so far (counted when an item sets a new bit); 0 for a missing key.

commands.name: BF.EXISTS
commands.limitations: RedisBloom wire shape; not certified module compatibility.

commands.name: BF.MEXISTS
commands.limitations: RedisBloom wire shape. A missing key answers 0 for every item.

commands.name: JSON.GET
commands.limitations: Optional path defaults to $. Supports only simple .field and [N] paths; not full RedisJSON.

commands.name: JSON.INDEX
commands.limitations: Ruvio extension (no RedisJSON/RediSearch equivalent): JSON.INDEX CREATE name PREFIX p PATH $.field [TYPE string|number|bool] | DROP name | LIST. Exact equality on one field only; database 0 only. Definitions are stored as reserved keys (visible to KEYS/DBSIZE) and dropped by FLUSHDB 0 / FLUSHALL; postings are rebuilt incrementally at startup.

commands.name: JSON.FIND
commands.limitations: Ruvio extension: JSON.FIND name VALUE v [COUNT n<=1000] [AFTER key] returns matching keys in ascending order; ERR index is building until the first build finishes. Runs on every shard and is merged.

commands.name: JSON.MGET
commands.limitations: One path for every key, as MGET: all keys must share a slot. A missing key or a key of another type gives null.

commands.name: JSON.SET
commands.limitations: Whole-document updates; only existing intermediate nodes; maximum resulting document 16 MiB. `NX` / `XX` as a fourth argument write only when the path is missing / present, and answer null otherwise. `EX seconds` or `PX milliseconds` sets a deadline only when the call creates the key; an existing key keeps its deadline. The write and the deadline are one WAL record. After the optional `NX` or `XX`.

commands.name: JSON.DEL
commands.limitations: Optional path defaults to $; returns 1 for a removed field, element, or root.

commands.name: XADD
commands.limitations: Auto id is * or ms-*. Explicit ids are ms-seq. DELAY holds the new entry from XREADGROUP until that many milliseconds pass. The hold is a WAL record and a snapshot trailer, written only when a delay is set. A millisecond behind the top id is rejected. MAXLEN and MINID, including ~ and =, both trim exactly. They cannot be combined. NOMKSTREAM returns a null bulk and does not create a missing key. The assigned id is the WAL record. The approximate trim option LIMIT is not accepted. `EX seconds` or `PX milliseconds` sets a deadline only when the call creates the key; an existing key keeps its deadline. The write and the deadline are one WAL record. Placed with the other options before the id.

commands.name: XLEN
commands.limitations: Returns 0 for a missing key.

commands.name: XRANGE
commands.limitations: start and end are -, +, or ms-seq. COUNT limits the reply. No exclusive bounds.

commands.name: XREVRANGE
commands.limitations: end then start, like Redis. COUNT keeps the newest matches. No exclusive bounds.

commands.name: XREAD
commands.limitations: COUNT and STREAMS. Id is exclusive; 0 means 0-0 and $ means the current end. BLOCK waits on this shard and does not remove entries. BLOCK 0 waits until an entry or shutdown. This command does not read a consumer group.

commands.name: XDEL
commands.limitations: Many ids. A repeated id counts once. The stream key and its last id remain after the last entry is deleted.

commands.name: XSETID
commands.limitations: Sets the last generated id without adding an entry. The id must be greater than or equal to the current top id. A missing key is an error. ENTRIESADDED and MAXDELETEDID are not accepted.

commands.name: XTRIM
commands.limitations: MAXLEN and MINID, including ~ and =, both trim exactly. MINID drops entries below the id and keeps that id. The approximate trim option LIMIT is not accepted.

commands.name: XGROUP CREATE
commands.limitations: Creates one group at $, 0, or an explicit id. MKSTREAM creates an empty stream when the key is missing.

commands.name: XGROUP CREATECONSUMER
commands.limitations: Registers a consumer before it has a pending entry. Returns 1 when the name is new and 0 when that group already has it. The name stays after its pending entries are acknowledged.

commands.name: XREADGROUP
commands.limitations: One stream and the > id only. COUNT limits the new entries. BLOCK waits on this shard until a later XADD and delivers that id to the oldest waiting consumer of the group. BLOCK 0 waits until an entry or shutdown. NOACK advances the group id and does not add a pending entry.

commands.name: XGROUP DESTROY
commands.limitations: Returns 1 when the group is removed and 0 when it is already gone. A blocked XREADGROUP on that group receives NOGROUP.

commands.name: XGROUP SETID
commands.limitations: Moves the group id to $, 0, or an explicit id. Pending entries stay as they are.

commands.name: XGROUP DELCONSUMER
commands.limitations: Returns how many pending entries that consumer held. A missing consumer returns 0. A missing group is NOGROUP.

commands.name: XACK
commands.limitations: Many ids. A repeated id counts once. Removes the id from that group's pending list and leaves the stream entry stored.

commands.name: XPENDING
commands.limitations: No arguments after the group returns the summary: count, smallest id, greatest id, and consumers sorted by name. An empty group returns 0, two nils, and an empty array. The extended form is optional IDLE, an inclusive start, an inclusive end, a count, and an optional consumer. Each row is the id, consumer, idle milliseconds, and delivery count.

commands.name: XAUTOCLAIM
commands.limitations: Scans pending ids after the start id. Claims those idle for at least min-idle milliseconds, up to COUNT, which defaults to the rest of the list. JUSTID returns ids. The reply is the next start id, the claimed entries, and ids dropped because the stream entry is gone. The next start id is 0-0 when the scan finishes.

commands.name: XCLAIM
commands.limitations: Claims pending ids idle for at least min-idle milliseconds. IDLE, TIME, RETRYCOUNT, FORCE, JUSTID, and LASTID are accepted. IDLE and TIME cannot be combined. FORCE claims an id that is in the stream but not pending and does not move the group cursor. LASTID sets that cursor. A repeated id is claimed once. An id deleted from the stream is dropped from the pending list and is not returned. JUSTID returns only the claimed ids.

commands.name: XINFO STREAM
commands.limitations: Reports length, last-generated-id, groups, and the first and last entries. Does not report a radix tree or entries-added. A missing key is an error.

commands.name: XINFO GROUPS
commands.limitations: Reports name, consumers, pending, last-delivered-id, and lag. Consumers are the distinct names on the pending list.

commands.name: XINFO CONSUMERS
commands.limitations: Lists pending consumers with pending count and idle time since the latest delivery. A consumer with an empty pending list is not stored.

commands.name: INFO
commands.limitations: INFO prometheus returns Prometheus text.

commands.name: WAIT
commands.limitations: Blocks only the calling client until N replicas have synced this shard's wal_last_sequence to disk, or the timeout. Timeout 0 waits until shutdown. The integer reply is how many replicas reached that sequence. A missing replica does not drop the write. Off and replica roles return 0. Not queued inside MULTI and not scriptable.

commands.name: REPLICAOF
commands.limitations: REPLICAOF host port makes every shard follow host:port (shard i dials port + i) without a restart; writes answer READONLY at once. A shard resumes from its own log when the new primary continues its history up to where it forked, otherwise it takes a full copy. REPLICAOF NO ONE promotes in place: queued frames are applied, a new history forks one epoch up, and the shard ships to replicas when replication.listen is set. It is refused while any shard has a catch-up marker unless FORCE is given; a shard still copying answers LOADING to every command, so an incomplete single-shard replica is promoted with a restart and --force-promote-incomplete. Durability memory and snapshot refuse it. Lasts until restart (the file's role applies again); not logged or replicated; refused inside MULTI and scripts. No SLAVEOF alias.

commands.name: ROLE
commands.limitations: Per shard (each shard is a node): a primary, or a server that does not replicate, answers master, its WAL sequence and its replicas that announced an address and finished copying ([host, port, acknowledged sequence], as strings); a replica answers slave, the address it dials, connect or connected, and its synced sequence.

commands.name: CONFIG GET
commands.limitations: Lists Ruvio settings with requirepass redacted; shows the live value of a setting CONFIG SET changed.

commands.name: CONFIG SET
commands.limitations: Live memory, observability, connection, script and security settings only (docs/CONFIGURATION.md, Live column); restart-only names such as shards, data_dir or TLS files are refused by name. Names as CONFIG GET shows them; values follow the config file's rules (plain byte counts, no 100mb units). All pairs apply or none. Every shard applies it before OK. Connection settings apply to new connections. Not written to the WAL, not replicated, not allowed in MULTI or scripts.

commands.name: CONFIG REWRITE
commands.limitations: Writes the live settings into the config file the server started from; restart-only settings keep what the file says. The file is rewritten as --write-config does (keys kept, comments dropped).

commands.name: SAVE
commands.limitations: In-process checkpoint.

commands.name: BGSAVE
commands.limitations: In-process, not a fork.

commands.name: MULTI
commands.limitations: Same-slot, shard-local only. At most 1,024 queued commands. EVAL, EVALSHA and FCALL queue and run in their place at EXEC, their writes in the transaction's one WAL record; a queued PUBLISH is sent after EXEC is recorded (DISCARD sends nothing). Not queueable: blocking commands, SELECT, SPUBLISH, SUBSCRIBE and the other subscribe commands, SCRIPT and FUNCTION management, AUTH, HELLO, ACL, CONFIG SET/REWRITE, SAVE/BGSAVE, REPLICAOF/ROLE and cluster discovery.

commands.name: EXEC
commands.limitations: A command refused while queueing (unknown, wrong arity, NOPERM, CROSSSLOT or MOVED, not allowed in MULTI, queue full) makes EXEC reply EXECABORT and discard the queue. Invalid arguments, such as MOVE or SWAPDB to a missing database, fail only that command at EXEC. One WAL Transaction record. Empty EXEC is *0; a dirty WATCH is *-1.

commands.name: DISCARD
commands.limitations: Drops the queue and leaves watches.

commands.name: WATCH
commands.limitations: At most 128 watched keys. A mutation by any connection, including the watcher, aborts EXEC.

commands.name: EVAL
commands.limitations: Lua 5.1 sandbox. Declared keys must be same-slot; a script with no keys runs on the connection's shard. Writes are one WAL batch.

commands.name: EVALSHA
commands.limitations: Cache is per shard and memory-only. Restart is NOSCRIPT. Same key rules as EVAL.

commands.name: SCRIPT LOAD
commands.limitations: Cache is not durable.

commands.name: SCRIPT KILL
commands.limitations: Returns NOTBUSY when no script is running.

commands.name: FCALL
commands.limitations: Runs a memory-only FUNCTION LOAD body. Same key rules as EVAL. Lua is not replayed.

commands.name: FUNCTION LOAD
commands.limitations: Stores one named Lua body on the shard. Not a Redis library shebang. Lost on restart.

commands.name: FUNCTION LIST
commands.limitations: Returns loaded function names in byte order.

commands.name: FUNCTION DELETE
commands.limitations: Removes one memory-only function. Returns 1 or 0.

commands.name: CLUSTER SLOTS
commands.limitations: Topology of the shards in one process, including ranges moved with RUVIO MOVESLOTS, and with cluster_topology the other groups of a multi-node cluster (by their primary). Hosts and ports come from advertised_host and advertised_port. Each range lists the primary shard, then its replicas that announced an address and finished copying; a replica lists the primary it follows first and itself second. Node ids are the SHA-1 of the announced host:port.

commands.name: CLUSTER NODES
commands.limitations: Static topology of the shards in one process. Hosts and ports come from advertised_host and advertised_port. Replicas that announced an address and finished copying appear as slave lines naming their primary's id.

commands.name: CLUSTER SHARDS
commands.limitations: Static topology of the shards in one process. Each shard lists its primary, then its replicas (role replica, replication-offset = acknowledged sequence).

commands.name: CLUSTER INFO
commands.limitations: cluster_state is always ok; every slot is assigned.

commands.name: CLUSTER MYID
commands.limitations: The id of the receiving shard.

commands.name: CLUSTER KEYSLOT
commands.limitations: Also available with one shard.

commands.name: RUVIO MOVESLOTS
commands.limitations: Ruvio only. RUVIO MOVESLOTS first-last shard (or one slot) moves a slot range to another shard of the same server while it keeps serving it, and answers OK once the move has started; RUVIO MOVESLOTS STATUS reports the running or last move as a map of strings (state none, copying, cleaning, cancelling, done or cancelled, and first, last, from, to, keys, rounds, elapsed_ms, freeze_ms, error). One move at a time; every slot of the range must be on one shard. Refused while replication is on and inside MULTI and scripts. No MOVED: clients that still route to the old shard are forwarded. A client blocked on a moved key gets UNBLOCKED, an EXEC whose watched keys moved runs nothing, and a pipelined command routed to the old shard at the hand-over may get TRYAGAIN.

commands.name: READONLY
commands.limitations: Returns OK in cluster mode. Replicas serve reads with or without it; clients send it to replica connections for Redis compatibility.

commands.name: READWRITE
commands.limitations: Returns OK in cluster mode; replicas refuse writes either way.

commands.name: SPUBLISH
commands.limitations: Delivered only to subscribers of that channel on this slot. Not stored and not durable. A full subscriber queue disconnects that subscriber.

commands.name: SSUBSCRIBE
commands.limitations: Puts the connection in Pub/Sub mode. Replies are RESP2 arrays. No pattern subscribe.

commands.name: SUNSUBSCRIBE
commands.limitations: No arguments unsubscribes every channel on this connection. An unknown channel still returns the current count.

commands.name: PUBLISH
commands.limitations: Delivers on this shard to exact SUBSCRIBE clients and matching PSUBSCRIBE patterns. Not stored and not written to the WAL. Other shards do not receive it. A full subscriber queue disconnects that subscriber.

commands.name: SUBSCRIBE
commands.limitations: Exact channels on this shard. The reply count is classic channels plus patterns on the connection. After a subscription the connection accepts SUBSCRIBE, UNSUBSCRIBE, PSUBSCRIBE, PUNSUBSCRIBE, SSUBSCRIBE, SUNSUBSCRIBE, and PING.

commands.name: UNSUBSCRIBE
commands.limitations: No arguments drops every exact classic channel on this connection and leaves patterns in place.

commands.name: PSUBSCRIBE
commands.limitations: Patterns use * and ?. Character classes are not supported. A match is delivered as pmessage. Keyspace notices stay on exact SSUBSCRIBE channels.

commands.name: PUNSUBSCRIBE
commands.limitations: No arguments drops every pattern on this connection and leaves exact channels in place.

commands.name: CLIENT GETNAME
commands.limitations: Empty when the connection has no name.

commands.name: CLIENT SETNAME
commands.limitations: An empty name clears it. The name is not durable.

commands.name: CLIENT DURABILITY
commands.limitations: Ruvio extension. CLIENT DURABILITY REPLICAS n [TIMEOUT ms] (default 5000 ms; n 0 turns it off): this connection's replies leave once n replicas hold on disk every record its shard wrote before them, checked once per batch of replies. On timeout every reply of the batch is -NOREPLICAS; the writes are applied and stay, as with WAIT. Refused inside MULTI and on a server without replication.

commands.name: CLIENT TRACKING
commands.limitations: ON or OFF only, and ON requires RESP3. Records GET and MGET on this shard, including misses. A completed write pushes one invalidate and forgets the key. No REDIRECT, BCAST, PREFIX, OPTIN, OPTOUT, or NOLOOP. Not cross-shard. A blocked BLPOP that pops later is not invalidated. A full push queue disconnects that connection.

commands.name: SSCAN
commands.limitations: Cursor is a position in member order. MATCH and COUNT are supported; a missing key returns cursor 0 and an empty array.

commands.name: ZSCAN
commands.limitations: Cursor is a position in score order. MATCH and COUNT are supported; a missing key returns cursor 0 and an empty array.

commands.name: JSON.MERGE
commands.limitations: RFC 7396 merge patch at a simple path; not RFC 6902 JSON Patch.

commands.name: JSON.TYPE
commands.limitations: Returns object, array, string, integer, number, boolean or null for the value at a simple path; null reply when the key or path is absent.

commands.name: JSON.STRLEN
commands.limitations: Byte length of a string value; WRONGTYPE for other values. Simple paths only.

commands.name: JSON.ARRLEN
commands.limitations: Element count of an array value; WRONGTYPE for other values. Simple paths only.

commands.name: JSON.OBJKEYS
commands.limitations: Object member names in document order; WRONGTYPE for other values. Simple paths only.

commands.name: JSON.NUMINCRBY
commands.limitations: Adds a number to a number value and returns the new value as a bulk string. Integer arithmetic when both are integers that do not overflow, otherwise a finite double. Logged as a path write of the computed value.

commands.name: JSON.TOGGLE
commands.limitations: Flips a boolean value and returns 1 for true, 0 for false. Logged as a path write.

commands.name: JSON.ARRAPPEND
commands.limitations: Appends one or more JSON values to an array and returns the new length. Logged as a path write of the whole array.

commands.name: JSON.CLEAR
commands.limitations: Empties an array or object, sets a number to 0, and returns how many values changed (0 when already empty or not clearable).

commands.name: JSON.OBJLEN
commands.limitations: Number of members of the object at the path; null when the key or path is missing.

commands.name: JSON.STRAPPEND
commands.limitations: `JSON.STRAPPEND key path json-string`. The path is required. Returns the new string length in bytes.

commands.name: JSON.NUMMULTBY
commands.limitations: `JSON.NUMMULTBY key path number`. The path is required. Integers stay integers unless the product overflows. A non-finite result is refused.

commands.name: JSON.ARRINSERT
commands.limitations: `JSON.ARRINSERT key path index value...`. A negative index counts from the end; an index outside 0..=length is an error. The path is required. Logged as a path write of the whole array.

commands.name: JSON.ARRPOP
commands.limitations: `JSON.ARRPOP key [path [index]]`. Default index -1; an index outside the array is clamped; an empty array answers null. Logged as a path write of the whole array.

commands.name: JSON.ARRTRIM
commands.limitations: `JSON.ARRTRIM key path start stop`, inclusive, negative from the end; a reversed or past-the-end range empties the array. Returns the new length.

commands.name: JSON.ARRINDEX
commands.limitations: `JSON.ARRINDEX key path scalar [start [stop]]`. Scalars only; a stop of 0 means the end; 1 and 1.0 are different values. Returns -1 when absent.

commands.name: JSON.FORGET
commands.limitations: Alias of JSON.DEL.

commands.name: JMERGE
commands.limitations: Alias of JSON.MERGE.

commands.name: COMMAND
commands.limitations: COMMAND, COMMAND COUNT, COMMAND INFO [name ...] and COMMAND DOCS [name ...] read the command table. INFO entries use the Redis 7 shape with empty tips, key specs and subcommands; DOCS entries are empty maps. Key positions and arity of Ruvio-native commands are informational.

commands.name: SETBIT
commands.limitations: Bitmap limited to 16 MiB (offset < 134,217,728); each call rewrites the value, O(value size). Keeps an existing TTL. `EX seconds` or `PX milliseconds` sets a deadline only when the call creates the key; an existing key keeps its deadline. The write and the deadline are one WAL record.

commands.name: BITFIELD
commands.limitations: GET, SET, INCRBY and OVERFLOW WRAP|SAT|FAIL on i1..i64 and u1..u63 fields (offset or #n). Field must end below 134,217,728 bits (16 MiB bitmap). A write rewrites the whole value, O(value size), and keeps an existing TTL.

commands.name: BITFIELD_RO
commands.limitations: GET only, same field types and limits as BITFIELD.

commands.name: GETBIT
commands.limitations: Offsets up to 2^32-1.

commands.name: BITOP
commands.limitations: AND, OR, XOR, NOT. Result limited to 16 MiB.

commands.name: PFADD
commands.limitations: Dense encoding only (12,304-byte string); every call rewrites the value. Estimates match Redis 7.

commands.name: PFCOUNT
commands.limitations: Multiple keys return the union estimate without storing it.

commands.name: PFMERGE
commands.limitations: The destination takes part in the union, as in Redis.

commands.name: FILLGET
commands.limitations: Ruvio command. Replies HIT, FILL, BUSY or STALE. Markers are memory only and expire after fill_ms. WAIT wait_ms holds a caller that would get BUSY (retry every 5 ms, like BLMOVE) until the filler writes, the marker lapses (the waiter then becomes the filler) or the wait ends with BUSY; it is refused inside MULTI and scripts.

commands.name: FILLSET
commands.limitations: Ruvio command. Needs the live token from FILLGET; SWR keeps the value stale_ms past its fresh period. The soft expiry is not persisted.

commands.name: SETEX
commands.limitations: Same as SET with EX.

commands.name: PSETEX
commands.limitations: Same as SET with PX.

commands.name: SETNX
commands.limitations: Returns 1 or 0.

commands.name: GETDEL
commands.limitations: Not a list or other type: WRONGTYPE.

commands.name: MSETNX
commands.limitations: All-or-nothing. Same-slot keys in multi-shard mode.

commands.name: INCRBYFLOAT
commands.limitations: Computed in double precision and printed with 16 significant digits and stored as that rounded text, so later increments start from the rounded value (use integers for money); Redis uses long double, so results with more digits can differ in the last places (Redis prints 153.10000000000000001 where Ruvio prints 153.1). Keeps the TTL. `EX seconds` or `PX milliseconds` sets a deadline only when the call creates the key; an existing key keeps its deadline. The write and the deadline are one WAL record.

commands.name: GETRANGE
commands.limitations: A range wholly before the start of the string returns an empty string (Redis 7.0 returns the first byte).

commands.name: SUBSTR
commands.limitations: Alias of GETRANGE.

commands.name: SETRANGE
commands.limitations: String limited to 16 MiB; each call rewrites the value, O(value size). Keeps the TTL.

commands.name: SINTERCARD
commands.limitations: Same-slot keys in multi-shard mode.

commands.name: ZUNIONSTORE
commands.limitations: Inputs may be sorted sets or sets (score 1). Same-slot keys in multi-shard mode. An empty result removes the destination.

commands.name: ZINTERSTORE
commands.limitations: Inputs may be sorted sets or sets (score 1). Same-slot keys in multi-shard mode. An empty result removes the destination.

commands.name: ZDIFFSTORE
commands.limitations: Same-slot keys in multi-shard mode. An empty result removes the destination.

commands.name: ZUNION
commands.limitations: Inputs may be sorted sets or sets (score 1). Same-slot keys in multi-shard mode. WITHSCORES is a flat array in both protocols.

commands.name: ZINTER
commands.limitations: Inputs may be sorted sets or sets (score 1). Same-slot keys in multi-shard mode. WITHSCORES is a flat array in both protocols.

commands.name: ZDIFF
commands.limitations: Same-slot keys in multi-shard mode. WITHSCORES is a flat array in both protocols.

commands.name: ZRANDMEMBER
commands.limitations: Pseudo-random; reads the whole set, O(N). WITHSCORES is a flat array in both protocols.

commands.name: HRANDFIELD
commands.limitations: Pseudo-random; reads the whole hash, O(N). WITHVALUES is a flat array in both protocols.

commands.name: HINCRBYFLOAT
commands.limitations: Computed in double precision and printed with 16 significant digits and stored as that rounded text, so later increments start from the rounded value (use integers for money; Redis uses long double). Keeps a field TTL.

commands.name: LINSERT
commands.limitations: Rewrites the list (O(N)); the WAL records the whole list as one atomic transaction.

commands.name: LSET
commands.limitations: Rewrites the list (O(N)); the WAL records the whole list as one atomic transaction.

commands.name: LREM
commands.limitations: Rewrites the list (O(N)); the WAL records the whole list as one atomic transaction.

commands.name: LPOS
commands.limitations: Read-only, O(N).

commands.name: LMOVE
commands.limitations: Atomic: the move is one WAL transaction.

commands.name: RPOPLPUSH
commands.limitations: ACL category and name follow LMOVE (`+lmove` allows it).

commands.name: BLMOVE
commands.limitations: Retries every 5 ms instead of parking a waiter; not allowed in MULTI or scripts. Counts against the 1,024 blocked-client limit.

commands.name: BLMPOP
commands.limitations: Retries every 5 ms instead of parking a waiter; not allowed in MULTI or scripts. Counts against the 1,024 blocked-client limit.

commands.name: KEYS
commands.limitations: Walks the database in one call, so it refuses databases above 100,000 keys per shard (use SCAN). Glob supports `*`, `?`, `[abc]`, `[^a-z]` and `\\` escapes. With several shards the arrays are joined.

commands.name: RANDOMKEY
commands.limitations: Starts at a pseudo-random slot of the key index, so it is not uniform. With several shards it picks a random non-nil answer.

commands.name: TOUCH
commands.limitations: Counts existing keys; does not update the access time used by eviction. Keys must share a shard, like EXISTS.

commands.name: COPY
commands.limitations: Strings, lists, sets, hashes and sorted sets, with their TTL. The `DB` option, streams, JSON, bloom filters and hashes with field TTLs are refused. Copies the whole value (O(N)) as one atomic WAL transaction.

commands.name: OBJECT
commands.limitations: `ENCODING`, `IDLETIME` and `FREQ` only. `ENCODING` names what Redis 7.0 would report (int, embstr, raw, quicklist, intset, hashtable, listpack, skiplist, stream), not the physical layout. `IDLETIME` needs an LRU `maxmemory-policy` and `FREQ` needs `allkeys-lfu`; otherwise they return an error (Redis tracks idle time under every policy). An unknown subcommand gets a generic error without the subcommand name.

commands.name: MEMORY
commands.limitations: `USAGE key [SAMPLES n]` only; the size is exact and counts the key, value and collection storage the memory budget charges, plus the fixed entry overhead. It is not comparable byte for byte with Redis.

commands.name: CLIENT ID
commands.limitations: Connection ids are per shard; with several shards two connections can share an id. Inside MULTI it answers at once instead of queueing.

commands.name: CLIENT LIST
commands.limitations: Each shard knows only its own connections; with several shards the reply covers the shard that got the command, and ids repeat across shards. Reports id, addr, laddr, name, age, db, multi, resp and user; `idle` is always 0 and the buffer and memory fields are left out. `TYPE` is validated but not used as a filter.

commands.name: CLIENT INFO
commands.limitations: The calling connection's `CLIENT LIST` line. Each shard knows only its own connections; with several shards the reply covers the shard that got the command, and ids repeat across shards.

commands.name: CLIENT KILL
commands.limitations: `ID`, `ADDR`, `SKIPME` and the legacy `addr` form; `USER`, `LADDR` and `TYPE` filters are refused. Each shard knows only its own connections; with several shards the reply covers the shard that got the command, and ids repeat across shards.

commands.name: SLOWLOG
commands.limitations: `GET`, `LEN`, `RESET`. Only commands that take the generic dispatcher are timed (not GET, SET, INCR, PING on the fast path) and blocking commands are skipped. An entry holds the command name and its first key (128 bytes), not every argument. Per shard; `slowlog_threshold_micros` and `slowlog_max_len` come from the config file or environment and CONFIG SET changes them live.

commands.name: LATENCY
commands.limitations: `LATEST` only, and it is always empty: Ruvio records no latency-spike events. Use `INFO latencystats`.

commands.name: DUMP
commands.limitations: Ruvio's own payload (`RVD1` plus a checksummed WAL record), not Redis RDB: only Ruvio's RESTORE reads it. Strings, lists, sets, hashes and sorted sets; streams, JSON, bloom filters and hashes with field TTLs are refused. The TTL is not part of the payload.

commands.name: RESTORE
commands.limitations: Reads only Ruvio's DUMP payload. `REPLACE` and `ABSTTL` work; `IDLETIME` and `FREQ` are accepted and ignored. A past `ABSTTL` deadline creates nothing. One atomic WAL transaction.
